articles.title: BYD no Brasil: Como o país virou laboratório de empresas chinesas | G1
articles.standfirst: Chegada da montadora à Bahia é simbólica dentro do contexto de ascensão da China ao posto de líder do mercado de veículos elétricos — e de aproximação econômica e cultural do país asiático com o Brasil. Reportagem da BBC News Brasil viajou a Camaçari para contar essa história global a partir das lentes locais.
articles.summary: A chegada da BYD no Brasil e sua fábrica em Camaçari simbolizam a liderança da China em carros elétricos e a nova aproximação econômica entre os países.
articles.body:
No início do ano circulou a informação — falsa — de que a Bahia sofria uma invasão chinesa. Vídeos compartilhados nas redes sociais mostravam a construção de um complexo de alojamentos que, na retórica da fake news , estaria sendo erguido para receber 10 mil chineses para trabalhar na recém-inaugurada fábrica da BYD.

Essa é a montadora chinesa que superou a Tesla de Elon Musk em 2025 e se tornou a maior produtora de veículos elétricos do mundo.

E escolheu Camaçari, na região metropolitana de Salvador, para sediar sua maior fábrica na América Latina.

Com parte do projeto ainda em obras, a planta foi inaugurada em outubro de 2025. Em menos de um ano, dela já saíram mais de 100 mil carros montados com kits importados, que chegaram a concessionárias em todo o país e alçaram a marca à lista das mais vendidas.

A produção made in Brasil está prevista para começar no fim de 2026. Ainda assim, a unidade já soma 7.618 funcionários diretos. Desse total, 6% (457) são estrangeiros, segundo a empresa. A reportagem apurou que a grande maioria são chineses.

Além deles, também há trabalhadores chineses envolvidos nas obras que estão em andamento, no complexo da fábrica e nos blocos de alojamentos para funcionários.

Nos registros da Polícia Federal constam a emissão de 2.310 vistos de residência em Camaçari e na vizinha Lauro de Freitas desde 2024, a maioria temporários.

BYD se tornou em 2025 a maior produtora de veículos elétricos do mundo. — Foto: Vitor Serrano/BBC

'Eles amam essa liberdade aqui da Bahia'

Em uma cidade de pouco mais de 300 mil habitantes, a presença chinesa não é óbvia. Não existe um bairro onde os recém-chegados se concentrem, uma Chinatown em Camaçari. Eles estão espalhados entre hotéis e alguns condomínios fechados.

Também não há uma onda de novos restaurantes tocados por imigrantes com foco na comunidade. Muitos funcionários da BYD comem no refeitório da própria fábrica, que tem uma área com pratos chineses e outra com receitas brasileiras, ou em casa.

A retórica predominante é a de que trabalham muito e circulam pouco: "A gente [brasileiro] chega em casa, toma um banho, deita no sofá, assiste televisão… Eles não, continuam trabalhando depois de chegar em casa. São muito reservados", diz a corretora Cássia Cotia, que vive em um condomínio em que mais de 60 imóveis estão alugados para chineses.

Os sinais sutis do novo fluxo migratório aparecem em locais como o mercado central de Camaçari — Foto: Vitor Serrano/BBC

Assim, as feições desse novo fluxo migratório se revelam aos poucos. No mercado central de Camaçari, entre bananas, camarões secos, café e tapioca, dois restaurantes que servem yakisoba agora têm placas escritas com ideogramas chineses. A comunidade de Testemunhas de Jeová local começou a fazer reuniões em mandarim recentemente.

Os "mais soltos", como descreve Cássia, se aventuram nos forrós e em outros pontos da vida noturna da cidade, e não raro vão parar nas redes sociais. Uma cena que viralizou recentemente no Camaforró mostrava uma moça ensinando um chinês a mexer os quadris e a legenda: "A China vai doutrinar o Brasil / O Brasil doutrinando a China".

Durante a visita à cidade, a reportagem da BBC News Brasil cruzou com um grupo animado tomando cerveja e comendo pizza em uma mesa na calçada na região da Praça dos 46, um dos locais onde a cidade se encontra no fim do dia para fazer caminhada, levar as crianças para brincar no parquinho e comer.

"Eles amam essa liberdade aqui da Bahia. Amam o calor humano", ressalta Cássia, que acabou virando amiga e uma espécie de concierge de muitos de seus clientes chineses, auxiliando-os a navegar tarefas mundanas como pagar contas ou encontrar um eletricista para fazer um reparo.

Eles se falam pelo WeChat, uma espécie de WhatsApp chinês. Ela envia as mensagens em português, eles recebem em mandarim. E agradecem com jantares cheios de iguarias chinesas e presentes sempre que alguém volta de viagem — uma das características mais marcantes da cultura chinesa na construção de relações.

"Eles me convidam… e eu já falei que tenho uma meta, em 2027, de conhecer a China."

São planos que ela nunca havia considerado fazer até pouco anos, quando era dona de um salão de beleza que era frequentado por funcionários de outra montadora: a Ford.

A corretora de imóveis Cássia Cotia hoje trabalha quase exclusivamente com chineses — Foto: Vitor Serrano/BBC

A presença da BYD no Brasil marca a ascensão da China à liderança do mercado automotivo global, e Camaçari é um lugar simbólico dessa virada: o local onde a montadora constrói sua fábrica na Bahia é o mesmo espaço físico ocupado por uma rival americana, a Ford, que fechou as portas em 2021.

Os Estados Unidos foram o berço da primeira grande revolução do setor automotivo, no início do século 20, quando Henry Ford introduziu a linha de montagem móvel e possibilitou a produção de carros em massa.

O pioneirismo garantiu a liderança do mercado aos americanos, até que vieram as concorrentes europeias e japonesas e também se consolidaram como marcas globais.

Até a virada para o século 21, a China não tinha qualquer protagonismo, mas aproveitou a transformação profunda que enxergava iminente no setor — a substituição dos carros a combustão pelos elétricos — como uma oportunidade para fazer sua ofensiva.

"Diferentemente de todas as outras regiões, a China apostou na eletrificação mais do que todo o mundo", aponta Rogélio Golfarb, que foi executivo da Ford no Brasil por décadas, presidente da Anfavea (Associação Nacional dos Fabricantes de Veículos Automotores) e hoje atua como consultor.

"Eles identificaram a possibilidade de ter uma vantagem competitiva e aí tiveram um programa de governo muito bem estruturado, que vinha desde a educação, pesquisa e desenvolvimento", acrescenta Golfarb.

A BYD é uma entre várias marcas de veículos elétricos que se desenvolveram nas últimas duas décadas dentro da lógica particular do capitalismo de estado chinês, com incentivos do governo e forte concorrência interna.

Foram elas que levaram a China a vencer o primeiro round da corrida global pela dominação do mercado de veículos elétricos, com uma fórmula baseada em quatro pilares: pioneirismo, foco na geração de inovação — em vez da mera cópia —, produção em larga escala e a verticalização, ou seja, a produção de quase tudo o que é preciso para colocar um carro na rua. É um modelo bastante diferente das montadoras tradicionais, que geralmente têm uma cadeia de fornecedores de partes e peças.

Essa combinação, ainda segundo Golfarb, deu aos elétricos e aos híbridos chineses uma competitividade enorme, justamente no momento em que Estados Unidos e Europa se fechavam cada vez mais aos produtos chineses.

Ainda em construção, blocos de alojamentos para funcionários da montadora em Camaçari viraram objeto de desinformação no início do ano — Foto: Vitor Serrano/BBC

Foi aí que a bússola apontou para a América Latina, e especialmente para o Brasil, um país de dimensões continentais, rico em matérias-primas usadas nas baterias dos carros, com abundante energia renovável e grande mercado consumidor.

"O Brasil hoje é o maior laboratório chinês que você tem no mundo no mercado automotivo. São mais de 20 marcas aqui", destaca Golfarb.

Além da BYD, vieram a GWM, que comprou a fábrica da Mercedes no Rio Grande do Sul, e a Geely, que firmou parceria com a Renault em São José dos Pinhais, no Paraná, entre outros.

"O novo carro popular brasileiro não é mais aquele carro a combustão. É o carro elétrico", afirma o ex-executivo da Ford.

"O carro que mais vende hoje é o Dolphin da BYD, que é o veículo elétrico. O sonho dos motoristas de Uber é ter um carro elétrico."

A competitividade das marcas chinesas acabou reduzindo os preços de automóveis de forma geral no Brasil.

Levantamento da consultoria automotiva Bright Consulting até junho de 2026 apontava que o preço de transação (pago pelos consumidores) de veículos leves novos havia caído 3,5%, para R$ 152,1 mil.

A queda foi atribuída ao aumento da concorrência de novas marcas, que em muitos casos "oferecem um nível de equipamentos significativamente superior ao dos concorrentes tradicionais, sem cobrança proporcional no preço".

Outra consequência é a mudança na percepção de parte dos brasileiros sobre os produtos chineses, por muito tempo vistos como cópias baratas e de baixa qualidade.

"Esse choque tecnológico e a velocidade com que eles trouxeram toda a linha de produtos neutralizou essa questão", opina Golfarb.

Conflitos trabalhistas têm crescido — Foto: Vitor Serrano/BBC

Dentro da fábrica, o ritmo mais acelerado é claro, na visão do presidente dos Sindicatos dos Metalúrgicos local, Júlio Bonfim.

"Eu tive a Ford, que teve 12 mil carros Courier enquanto treinava o pessoal durante dois anos e produzindo depois. A BYD já está produzindo, trocando o pneu com o carro a 180 quilômetros por hora", ilustra.

Segundo ele, os conflitos trabalhistas têm crescido na mesma cadência.

"O assédio moral hoje é um problema sério dentro da BYD", diz Bonfim, emendando que têm se multiplicado as reclamações de funcionários queixando-se de pressão e tratamento grosseiro.

"Por uma questão cultural, pela concepção que é passada da cultura chinesa para os líderes brasileiros, eles acabam se comportando como capitães do mato, perseguindo e assediando moralmente os trabalhadores", acrescenta.

O Ministério Público do Trabalho chegou a abrir procedimento para investigar as alegações do sindicato de ocorrência de assédio moral e sexual, mas o arquivou recentemente sob a justificativa de falta de provas.

A reportagem da BBC News Brasil buscou por dois meses pedir autorização para entrar na fábrica, mas a BYD não permitiu a visita. Também procuramos funcionários, mas eles evitam conversar com a imprensa por medo de represálias.

Em nota, a BYD afirmou que "não tolera qualquer forma de assédio, discriminação ou conduta que viole a lei". Também disse que "mantém canais internos que permitem denúncias de forma confidencial e anônima e trata com seriedade todo relato recebido, com apuração e adoção das medidas cabíveis".

Comparando passado e presente, o presidente do sindicato dos metalúrgicos lembra que nos primeiros anos da Ford também houve conflitos, especialmente em relação à remuneração e condições de trabalho e, segundo ele, por diversos episódios de xenofobia.

"Eles achavam que a gente só sabia fazer acarajé, dormir em rede, estereótipo equivocado que no Sul-Sudeste é passado do nordestino, do baiano que é preguiçoso, que só sabe dormir em rede e tomar água de coco", ressalta Bonfim.

A vantagem, naquele caso, era que a Ford chegava à Bahia tendo passado pela experiência do movimento sindical americano — a combativa United Auto Workers (UAW) — e do movimento sindical brasileiro no ABC Paulista.

Ele relata que, depois de uma série de greves entre 2004 e 2007, a relação com a empresa melhorou, assim como as condições de trabalho no chão de fábrica. A Ford chegou a produzir 250 mil carros no pico, mas teve que diminuir o ritmo a partir de 2013, quando a economia desacelerou. O cenário de crise se aprofundou com a pandemia de covid-19 e em 2021, a montadora decidiu fechar as portas. Desativou todas as fábricas no país.

Para Bonfim, a situação agora é diferente também por uma particularidade da China, um país com regime autoritário e sem liberdade sindical.

"É muito difícil para os chineses entenderem o movimento sindical brasileiro porque eles não têm sindicato na China. Na China o sindicato é o próprio governo", afirma.

O sindicato fez a primeira paralisação na BYD em julho de 2026, durante uma assembleia em frente à fábrica. 2700 trabalhadores voltaram para casa, segundo ele, em protesto contra a notificação de dois dirigentes sindicais.

Ainda durante a construção da fábrica, no fim de 2024, 163 cidadãos chineses foram resgatados do trabalho em condições análogas à escravidão no canteiro de obras da BYD.

"Essa história já é bem conhecida, nós identificamos o tráfico de pessoas por trabalho escravo, retenção de passaporte, restrição de liberdade de comoção, vigilância armada nos alojamentos, condição degradante, alojamentos superlotados, ausência de colchão", relembra Luciano Aragão, coordenador nacional de erradicação do trabalho escravo e enfrentamento ao tráfico de pessoas do Ministério Público do Trabalho (MPT).

"Ausência de conforto térmico, um banheiro para uma quantidade imensa de trabalhadores, comida armazenada de forma completamente inadequada, inclusive em portas de banheiros no canteiro de obras", acrescenta.

A BBC News Brasil mostrou em reportagem os bastidores da operação. Na ocasião, a empresa não se manifestou sobre o caso. Procurada novamente, comunicou: "Em dezembro de 2025, foi firmado acordo com Ministério Público do Trabalho para encerrar o processo relacionado aos fatos apurados no ano anterior. Pelo acordo, as empreiteiras terceirizadas concordaram em pagar integralmente o valor de R$ 40 milhões. O caso foi solucionado por acordo, sem julgamento de mérito ou condenação judicial."

Número de autorizações de residência para trabalho emitidas para cidadãos chineses no Brasil triplicou entre 2023 e 2025, para 10 mil — Foto: Vitor Serrano/BBC

'Eles querem aprender português pra vir pra cá'

O mercado automotivo é só um dos canais que têm aproximado o Brasil à China. Em 2025 o país foi o principal destino de investimentos chineses no mundo, concentrando 10,9% dos quase US$ 60 bilhões, conforme os dados do Conselho Empresarial Brasil-China (CEBC).

São muitos os fatores que tornam o Brasil atrativo para o capital chinês, diz o diretor de conteúdo e pesquisa do CEBC, Tulio Cariello. O país tem grande mercado consumidor, é aberto ao investimento estrangeiro, tem abundância de energias limpas — um elemento importante para a indústria chinesa, que está tentando se descarbonizar —, e mão de obra qualificada.

"Já ouvi de empresários chineses que vêm para cá falando muito bem dos engenheiros [brasileiros], dos quadros técnicos de forma geral", acrescenta.

"A gente oferece tantas vantagens em um mundo que está se fechando para a China, que é praticamente impossível a China não querer vir para cá", completa.

O aumento da presença de empresas chinesas também fez crescer o fluxo migratório de forma mais ampla para o país. Entre 2023 e 2025 triplicou o número de autorizações de residência para trabalho emitidas para cidadãos chineses no Brasil, de 3 mil para 10 mil no ano passado.

Diante desse cenário, é crescente o interesse de chineses pelo português brasileiro, conta Alice Oliveira, cientista social que acabou se tornando professora de português para chineses depois de fazer parte, em 2023, da primeira turma de ensino de mandarim do então recém-aberto Instituto Confúcio em Salvador.

A organização promove a língua e a cultura chinesas e é vinculado ao governo da China. Já são 14 espalhados pelo país, um sintoma de um movimento que vai além das cifras de investimento e reflete uma tentativa de aproximação cultural com o Brasil.

Alice já estava concluindo o curso de Ciências Sociais — e infeliz com a perspectiva de passar parte da carreira na área de pesquisa — quando entrou no curso e se apaixonou pelo mandarim.

Já teve cinco alunos chineses, um deles vendedor de máquinas que trabalha com outro grande projeto chinês na Bahia, a ponte Salvador-Itaparica, que, quando concluída, deve se tornar a maior ponte sobre lâmina d'água da América Latina.

Até pouco tempo, ela conta, os chineses costumavam aprender português com sotaque de Portugal, em muito por conta da proximidade com Macau, uma pequena ilha ao sul da China que é ex-colônia portuguesa.

Era comum aprender o idioma para ir para Moçambique e Angola, que nas últimas décadas têm estreitado laços com a China.

"Agora, porém, com aproximação Brasil e China, o pessoal tá querendo aprender português brasileiro pra vir pra cá."

A ligação cada vez mais forte entre os dois países acabou virando objeto da rixa ideológica entre direita e esquerda no Brasil, especialmente com a consolidação da China como grande rival dos Estados Unidos e com a volta de Donald Trump à Casa Branca. A fake news dos 10 mil chineses invadindo Camaçari teve como origem essa disputa e foi replicada por diversos perfis em março deste ano.

Quem quer que vença o segundo turno, entretanto, terá de navegar esse cenário em que EUA e China, as duas maiores potências do mundo hoje — e os dois maiores parceiros comerciais do país — olham para um Brasil que pode ser estratégico, como mercado consumidor, fornecedor de alimentos e produtor de terras raras.

"O período de vinculação a uma superpotência ou a outra passou", opina Wendel Henrique Baumgartner, professor do departamento de Geografia da Universidade Federal da Bahia (UFBA).

"Temos que tomar muito cuidado para que a gente não mude a dependência que tínhamos no período colonial da Europa, que depois foi substituída pelos Estados Unidos, para agora criar uma dependência com a China. Eu acho que a gente tem que ser muito estratégico e abrir as portas para o mundo", avalia o professor, emendando que hoje o país tem a possibilidade de escolher e que, por isso, não deveria escolher entre um lado ou outro.

"Precisamos escolher o Brasil, e entender que é importante para o Brasil vender seus produtos, receber esses investimentos, melhorar sua infraestrutura, diversificar ainda mais o parque industrial e, principalmente, desenvolver tecnologia. Não só importar tecnologia, mas usar essa esses recursos que estão chegando em abundância no Brasil para que a gente desenvolva tecnologia própria."

articles.body:
Morre monsenhor Antônio Ordones Lemos — Foto: Diocese de Divinópolis/Divulgação

O monsenhor Antônio Ordones Lemos morreu aos 86 anos, na madrugada desta terça-feira (20), em Divinópolis . Segundo a Diocese, desde 2022 ele estava em estágio avançado da doença de Alzheimer.

Conforme ainda a Diocese, o velório será na Paróquia Nossa Senhora da Guia, a partir das 9h. A Missa de Exéquias está marcada para 11h.

🔎 Missa de Exéquias: é a liturgia cristã dos funerais, celebrada como expressão do mistério pascal morte e ressurreição de Cristo.

O monsenhor faleceu na Casa de Repouso Terça da Serra em Divinópolis, onde residia há alguns anos.

Sua última paróquia na cidade foi a São José Operário, onde exerceu a função de vigário. Ele também atuou na Paróquia Nossa Senhora da Guia.

O monsenhor Antônio Ordones Lemos nasceu no dia 16 de junho de 1940 em Campos Altos , no Triângulo Mineiro.

Foi ordenado padre no dia 3 de fevereiro de 1968 na Catedral Divino Espírito Santo, em Divinópolis, pelo então bispo da época, Dom Cristiano Frederico Portela de Araújo Pena.

articles.title: Felca: relembre relato sobre ansiedade social no Fantástico  | G1
articles.standfirst: Criador de conteúdo falou sobre a dificuldade de se relacionar com pessoas na série "Sobre Nós". Nesta terça-feira (20), ele voltou ao tema ao relatar o diagnóstico de fobia social em novo vídeo no YouTube.
articles.summary: Criador de conteúdo falou sobre a dificuldade de se relacionar com pessoas na série "Sobre Nós".
articles.body:
O influenciador Felipe Bressanim Pereira, conhecido como Felca, publicou nesta terça-feira (20) um novo vídeo no YouTube , o primeiro desde que lançou “Adultização”, produção que viralizou em 2025 e impulsionou o debate nacional sobre a proteção de crianças e adolescentes na internet.

Desta vez, Felca deixou de lado o formato investigativo para falar sobre a própria história. No vídeo, ele fala sobre o diagnóstico de fobia social e anuncia um desafio pessoal para enfrentar o medo de interações sociais.

O relato retoma um tema que o influenciador já havia abordado no Fantástico , em março, na série “Sobre Nós”, dedicada à saúde mental e aos desafios que afetam principalmente os jovens.

No episódio, Felca falou sobre ansiedade social e a dificuldade de lidar com situações que envolvem outras pessoas.

“Eu tenho medo de pessoas. Eu gosto de sair de casa, mas, quando me chamam, torço para cancelarem. E, quando vou, fico pensando em como me portar: vou dançar? Como vou dançar? Que roupa usar? Eu queria que fosse cancelado”, disse o influenciador.

Na reportagem, um especialista explica que o medo e a ansiedade são emoções naturais, que funcionam como alertas diante de situações percebidas como ameaçadoras. No caso da ansiedade social, a dificuldade está relacionada ao receio de interagir com outras pessoas e de ser avaliado negativamente.

“Somos animais sociais. Nossa sobrevivência sempre dependeu da capacidade de viver em grupo”, afirma. "Para grande parte das pessoas, é desafiador estar em contato com alguém novo ou se colocar numa situação em que vc possa ser avaliado negativamente. Ou julgado".

Veja a reportagem completa no vídeo acima.

Nova série com Felca aborda saúde mental entre jovens — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

A série “Sobre Nós” foi dividida em seis episódios, com discussões sobre temas como insegurança, pressão em relação ao futuro e relações sociais. Ao longo da produção, Felca também conversou com especialistas sobre comportamento e bem-estar emocional.

O podcast Isso É Fantástico está disponível no g1 e nos principais aplicativos de podcasts, trazendo grandes reportagens, investigações e histórias fascinantes em podcast com o selo de jornalismo do Fantástico: profundidade, contexto e informação. articles.title: Exército ucraniano faz salvamento inédito de soldado ferido com drone | G1
articles.standfirst: Presença de drones inimigos e o fato de a área ter sido dominada pelas forças adversárias impediram que ele fosse retirado pelo método habitualmente utilizado, com sistemas terrestres. Militar foi transportado até um ponto de evacuação e está em tratamento e reabilitação.
articles.summary: Presença de drones inimigos e o fato de a área ter sido dominada pelas forças adversárias impediram que ele fosse retirado pelo método habitualmente utilizado.
articles.body:
Ucrânia usa drone para resgatar soldado ferido na linha de frente da guerra contra a Rússia em outubro de 2026. — Foto: Divulgação/Exército da Ucrânia

Um soldado ucraniano ferido foi resgatado com a ajuda de um drone aéreo em uma operação inédita na linha de frente da guerra, segundo as Forças Terrestres da Ucrânia.

O militar foi transportado até um ponto de evacuação e está em tratamento e reabilitação. Ele não corre mais risco de vida.

De acordo com o exército ucraniano, o soldado foi ferido enquanto estava em uma posição militar. A presença de drones inimigos e o fato de a área ter sido dominada pelas forças adversárias impediram que ele fosse retirado pelo método habitualmente utilizado, com um sistema robótico terrestre.

Para realizar o resgate, os militares utilizaram um hexacóptero pesado, um tipo de drone com seis rotores, fornecido gratuitamente por um fabricante ucraniano.

Integrantes do exército trabalharam com a empresa para adaptar o equipamento às exigências da missão e garantir a estabilidade durante o transporte do ferido.

Militar ucraniano ferido é salvo por drone. — Foto: Reprodução

Após testes preliminares, a operação foi realizada com a participação de diferentes unidades das Forças Terrestres ucranianas.

“Foi uma operação extremamente difícil, mas bem-sucedida. É um acontecimento histórico, uma nova etapa na evacuação de feridos à qual todos chegaremos. Agora começa um trabalho sério e sistemático para que missões como essa sejam realizadas continuamente”, afirmou Napalm, comandante de esquadra e programador de uma companhia de sistemas robóticos terrestres do exército ucraniano.

Ainda segundo o exército ucraniano, o soldado ferido continuou combatendo os ataques inimigos mesmo enquanto aguardava o resgate, em condições consideradas extremamente difíceis.

Os militares ucranianos afirmam que a missão abre caminho para a realização contínua de evacuações aéreas de feridos e para a ampliação do uso de drones nas operações militares.

articles.title: US government bans American technology company from Green Card programme for two years; fines $1.4 million; DOJ says: Violated Immigration and Nationality Act by …
articles.summary: US government has banned Cloudera, a Santa Clara, California-based data management company from participating in the Permanent Labor Certification (PERM)
articles.body: US government has banned Cloudera, a Santa Clara, California-based data management company from participating in the Permanent Labor Certification (PERM) program for two years. For those unaware, PERM is the required first step for US employers to sponsor a foreign worker for a permanent employment-based green card. In a press release, the Department of Justice said that it has imposed a fine of $1.4 million on Cloudera Cloudera for violating the Immigration and Nationality Act (INA) by discriminating against U.S. workers when recruiting and hiring for seven positions under the PERM process. "Cloudera will establish a back-pay fund of $1.4 million to compensate qualified U.S. workers who tried to apply for the jobs at issue but were not given fair consideration. Cloudera also will pay $600,000 in civil penalties to the United States," the department said.“There are no exceptions: the Justice Department will hold accountable employers who discriminate against U.S. workers,” said Assistant Attorney General Harmeet K. Dhillon of the Justice Department’s Civil Rights Division. “This substantial settlement, in partnership with DOL, sends a strong signal to employers that the federal government will work together to ensure employers treat U.S. workers fairly.”The debarment follows DOL’s earlier suspension of Cloudera’s PERM processing and reflects DOL’s commitment to aggressively enforcing labor certification requirements when employers fail to provide US workers a fair opportunity to compete for jobs.What the Justice department said banning Cloudera from PERMIn the official release, DOJ said:“The U.S. Department of Justice’s Civil Rights Division (CRT) and the U.S. Department of Labor (DOL) today announced a coordinated enforcement resolution with Cloudera Inc., a Santa Clara, California-based data management company, following allegations that the company discriminated against qualified U.S. workers during recruitment conducted under the Permanent Labor Certification (PERM) program.“There are no exceptions: the Justice Department will hold accountable employers who discriminate against U.S. workers,” said Assistant Attorney General Harmeet K. Dhillon of the Justice Department’s Civil Rights Division. “This substantial settlement, in partnership with DOL, sends a strong signal to employers that the federal government will work together to ensure employers treat U.S. workers fairly.”As part of the resolution, Cloudera will be barred from participating in the PERM program for two years, one of the most significant sanctions available for DOL to protect the integrity of the employment-based immigration system and safeguard opportunities for U.S. workers. The debarment follows DOL’s earlier suspension of Cloudera’s PERM processing and reflects DOL’s commitment to aggressively enforcing labor certification requirements when employers fail to provide U.S. workers a fair opportunity to compete for jobs.The settlement also resolves a lawsuit DOJ filed in April of this year, alleging that Cloudera violated the Immigration and Nationality Act (INA) by discriminating against U.S. workers when recruiting and hiring for seven positions under the PERM process. Under the terms of the settlement with the Justice Department, Cloudera will establish a back-pay fund of $1.4 million to compensate qualified U.S. workers who tried to apply for the jobs at issue but were not given fair consideration. Cloudera also will pay $600,000 in civil penalties to the United States.In addition to the two-year debarment, Cloudera will be subject to compliance obligations designed to ensure future adherence to federal labor and anti-discrimination laws. These measures include enhanced monitoring, revised PERM compliance procedures, and reporting requirements intended to prevent future violations.This debarment and compliance framework establish an important enforcement precedent and strengthen future efforts to protect U.S. workers. The PERM program allows employers to sponsor aliens for permanent residence only after demonstrating that qualified U.S. workers were provided a genuine opportunity to apply and that no qualified, willing, and available U.S. workers could be found. Employers who evade these requirements undermine both program integrity and the interests of U.S. workers. This resolution is one of many examples of coordinated federal enforcement designed to ensure employers comply with labor market protections established by Congress.This settlement is also the fourteenth settlement since DOJ re-launched its Protecting U.S. Workers Initiative in 2025 to enforce the INA’s prohibition on citizenship status discrimination against companies that illegally discriminate against U.S. workers in favor of those with temporary employment visas. Under these settlements, DOJ obtains civil penalties for each violation and will continue to appropriately seek the maximum penalty permitted by law. The settlements also involve awards of back pay, when warranted, and require employers to conduct comprehensive training for relevant staff and recruiters and cease restricting consideration for job opportunities based on workers’ citizenship status without a lawful reason."You use AI every day. articles.summary: A Kenyan doomsday cult leader linked to the deaths of more than 400 people has been convicted of murdering 190 children and one adult.
articles.body: A Kenyan doomsday cult leader linked to the deaths of more than 400 people has been convicted of murdering 190 children and one adult.Justice Diana Kavedza ruled on Monday that cult leader Mackenzie, leader of the Good News International Church, used religious teachings to make his followers fast until they died. In her ruling, Justice Kavedza said that “medical treatment was presented as an instrument of Satan”.Prosecutors said Paul Mackenzie ordered his followers to starve themselves to death to meet Jesus. Mackenzie’s followers lived in mud huts on the 800-acre property, away from nearby communities and authorities.Mackenzie was arrested and charged with murder along with his wife and dozens of followers. Some followers later became witnesses for the prosecution. The trial began in 2023.In May 2024, the High Court had ordered prosecutors to reduce the charges to no more than 12. articles.title: A New York entrepreneur pitched his high-protein lupini bean pizzas to stores from a Citi Bike; after launching in 2025, his brand Loopini surpassed $700,000 in revenue by April 2026
articles.summary: Damiano Messineo turned his passion for food and business into Loopini, a high-protein pizza brand made with lupini beans that has grown from one New York
articles.body: Damiano Messineo turned his passion for food and business into Loopini, a high-protein pizza brand made with lupini beans that has grown from one New York City store to major retail chains. The Italian entrepreneur began developing the product in 2024, using a spreadsheet to create his ideal nutritional label before experimenting with ingredients in his kitchen.After launching in January 2025, he travelled around New York City on a Citi Bike, pitching the pizzas to independent shops and delivering orders himself. The business later entered Whole Foods, Wegmans, and Target. In a 2026 interview with Entrepreneur, Messineo shared that Loopini had surpassed $700,000 in revenue by April.How Damiano Messineo built Loopini into a high-protein pizza brandMessineo wanted to create a food business in the United States that combined his interest in entrepreneurship with his love of pizza. Rather than opening a restaurant, he chose to develop a consumer product that could grow at scale. His idea was to make pizza a healthier option that people could eat regularly without viewing it as junk food.In 2024, he used an Excel spreadsheet to develop a nutritional label that suited his goals for a meal. He tested different ingredients from around the world before discovering lupini beans. Although he came from southern Italy, where the beans are widely consumed, he had not eaten many of them while growing up. Research showed him that they were rich in protein and fibre and contained all nine essential amino acids. He also noted their low glycaemic index and mineral content.From a home kitchen to 50 independent stores in New York CityThe early versions of Loopini's pizza tasted terrible, and it took several months of experimentation to get the recipe right. By October 2024, Messineo and his co-founder, Alessandro Pignataro, had created a minimum viable product. They initially planned to manufacture in the United States but chose Italy because Messineo had stronger connections there. The founders partnered with a small contract manufacturer and launched Loopini in New York City in January 2025. Pop Up Grocer became the brand's first store.Messineo then travelled around the city on a Citi Bike, approaching independent shops and delivering pizzas himself. The approach helped the business expand from one store to 50 independent retailers over a couple of months. Instead of accepting an early distribution deal, the founders chose to wait until they had greater bargaining power. They entered pitch competitions and won almost every one they took part in.Whole Foods, Wegmans and Target helped Loopini surpass $700,000Loopini raised a pre-seed funding round in January 2026. At the time of the interview, Messineo and Pignataro were still the company's only team members. The business entered its first retail chain, Whole Foods, in January 2026, initially across the Northeast and North Atlantic. A month later, it launched in every Wegmans store. In March, Loopini entered Target, with its products first reaching stores in the Northeast before a nationwide rollout.The company generated $100,000 in revenue in 2025. By April 2026, its revenue had reached $700,000. Loopini had also received offers for national expansion, while other major retailers had expressed interest. The founders were considering these opportunities while focusing on production capacity and product quality before expanding further across the country.Damiano Messineo ate Loopini pizza for around 100 days while training for an IronmanMessineo first tested the pizza by eating it for 30 consecutive days in July 2024. After the product hit the market, he decided to run a longer experiment to gather more data on its effects on his body. He ate Loopini pizza for around 100 days, from January 13 to April 26, while tracking physical measurements, blood tests, and stool tests. He also trained for an Ironman to examine whether the product could fuel an endurance athlete.Messineo reported losing four pounds of fat and gaining six pounds of muscle during the challenge. His score, based on 150 biomarkers, rose from 81 out of 100 before the challenge to 89 afterwards. He also completed his first Ironman in Lima, Peru, in five hours and 42 minutes.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: As Ravana's effigies burn across India, his ‘descendants’ in Jodhpur gather to mourn him
articles.summary: JODHPUR: As Ravana’s towering effigies go up in flames across India on Dussehra, a small community in Rajasthan’s Jodhpur does something that sets it
articles.body: JODHPUR: As Ravana’s towering effigies go up in flames across India on Dussehra, a small community in Rajasthan’s Jodhpur does something that sets it apart from the celebrations around it.Its members wait for the fires to die down, bathe, change their sacred threads and gather at a temple to offer prayers to the very king whose death the festival commemorates.For the Dave Godha community, a gotra of Shrimali Brahmins who consider themselves descendants of Ravana, Dussehra is not a celebration of his defeat but a day of mourning and remembrance.“We worship Ravana and try to imbibe his good qualities,” says Kamlesh Kumar Dave, chief priest of the community’s temple near Mehrangarh Fort. For the families who follow this tradition, Ravana is not merely the ten-headed king cast as the embodiment of evil in popular retellings of the Ramayana. They revere him as a learned ruler, a master musician and a scholar of the Vedas.Their observance begins after the customary Ravana Dahan is over. Male members of the community take a bath, change their janeu, the sacred thread worn by Brahmins, and assemble at the temple for special prayers. Flowers, sweets and food offerings are made as they seek peace for Ravana’s soul.“Even though Ravana Dahan may not take place, we have always observed mourning on this day, and this year too, we will do the same,” Dave has said of the annual ritual.The practice rests on a local legend that places Ravana’s marriage to Mandodari in Mandore, now a garden suburb about 11km from Jodhpur. According to the belief, Mandodari was the daughter of Mayasura, the king associated with Mandawar, and Ravana travelled from Lanka with a wedding procession, or baraat, to marry her.Dave says some members of Ravana’s wedding party stayed behind after the marriage, eventually giving rise to the community that now claims him as its forefather.“When he came to Mandor to tie the knot with Mandodari, many of his relatives accompanied his ‘baraat’ from Lanka to Mandor. After the marriage, Ravana returned to his kingdom with his queen but some of his relatives stayed here,” he says.The legend has endured across generations, shaping a tradition that runs counter to the dominant symbolism of Vijayadashami — the triumph of good over evil. For the community, remembering Ravana means looking beyond the familiar narrative of his abduction of Sita and his eventual defeat by Lord Rama.“Beyond his image as Sita’s abductor, he was a veena virtuoso and a sage whose mastery of mantras could command nature,” says Ajay Dave, Kamlesh Dave’s son. He also describes Ravana as a scholar whose knowledge of the Vedas and Puranas earned him reverence.The community’s temple, built in 2008 at the foot of Mehrangarh Fort, gives this belief a permanent home. Before its construction, families worshipped Ravana at their homes. The temple now houses idols of Ravana and Mandodari, along with Kharanana, regarded as the community’s kuldevi, or clan deity. The statues depict Ravana worshipping Lord Shiva.Around 100 Dave Godha families live in Jodhpur, mainly in the old-city localities of Chandpol and Brahmpuri. Other families of the clan are also reported to live in Phalodi district.The temple’s daily worship continues beyond Dussehra, with musicians and students of the Vedas among those who visit to seek Ravana’s blessings. For the community, his reputation as a scholar and musician remains central to the way he is remembered.In Mandore, the landscape itself is woven into the story. A spot on Mandore hill is known locally as Ravana’s Chanwari, believed to be where the wedding vows were exchanged. The legend also links the area to Mayasura and Mandodari, whose story is passed down as part of the region’s cultural lore.Mandore later became a capital of Marwar under the Rathore dynasty before the rulers shifted their capital to Jodhpur in 1459. Its gardens remain a popular attraction today.But for the Dave Godha families, Mandore holds a significance beyond its history and gardens. It is the place where, according to their tradition, their ancestor’s story began — and where a wedding legend helps explain why a day of public celebration is observed in their homes and temple as one of mourning.Stay updated with the latest Jodhpur news. articles.title: France looks to give Rafale anti-radar punch with new Hammer variant
articles.summary: France is looking to equip its Rafale fighters with a new variant of the AASM Hammer precision-guided weapon, to fill a long-standing gap in its ability
articles.body: France is looking to equip its Rafale fighters with a new variant of the AASM Hammer precision-guided weapon, to fill a long-standing gap in its ability to suppress and destroy enemy air defences, according to reports. The proposed Hammer XLR uses a miniature turbojet engine instead of the solid-fuel rocket motor on existing variants, which could give French aircraft an extended-range option for striking targets in heavily defended airspace. General Jérôme Bellanger, chief of staff of the French Air and Space Force, highlighted the weapon's potential while testifying to the National Assembly on October 14, according to the French defence website Opex360. The report said it could restore a capability France lost when it retired the AS-37 Martel anti-radiation missile in the 1990s, and that the variant is expected to become operational by 2028.The development matters to India because the Indian Air Force already flies the standard Hammer on its Rafales. The weapon, whose name stands for Armement Air-Sol Modulaire (AASM), or Highly Agile Modular Munition Extended Range (HAMMER), is a modular air-to-ground weapon developed by Safran. It combines a guidance system, a warhead and a range-extension kit, which lets conventional bombs be turned into precision-guided munitions, and its propulsion allows release from a distance instead of overflying the target.India chose the Hammer in 2020, when it was trying to get its Rafale fleet operational quickly amid tensions with China along the Line of Actual Control. It was not part of the original 2016 weapons package, and reports said the IAF had first considered integrating Israel's SPICE 2000. The Hammer was picked because it was already compatible with the French fighter and could be integrated faster. The IAF's inventory also includes the SCALP air-launched cruise missile and the SPICE family of guided munitions.The XLR would add a different mission, Suppression of Enemy Air Defences (SEAD) involves disrupting or neutralising radar systems and surface-to-air missile batteries, while Destruction of Enemy Air Defences (DEAD) focuses on physically destroying them, and both help create safer corridors for other aircraft. The Rafale already carries the SPECTRA electronic warfare suite, which detects, identifies and responds to threats, but electronic self-protection does not replace a dedicated weapon that can home in on hostile radar emissions. In February 2026, Bharat Electronics Limited and Safran signed a joint venture agreement and a master production agreement to make, supply and maintain the Hammer in India, subject to approvals, to meet the needs of the IAF and the Navy, with localisation rising in phases.The XLR remains a reported French development and not an Indian procurement. Any Indian acquisition would need separate confirmation, and the immediate benefit for India lies in the existing Hammer and its planned domestic production line.India already operates anti-radiation weapons, including the Russian Kh-31 family, and has been developing its own through the Defence Research and Development Organisation. Rudram-I, the first indigenous anti-radiation missile, was flight-tested from a Su-30MKI in October 2020. It uses inertial navigation aided by satellite navigation and a passive homing head that can detect, classify and engage radar emissions, so aircraft need not approach defended areas. The programme has since moved to the Rudram-II air-to-surface missile. The DRDO and the IAF conducted flight tests in June 2026, and the Defence Ministry said the missiles were guided to predefined targets and all test objectives were met. Rudram-II is meant to engage a wider range of targets, including radar-related installations and other military assets.

articles.title: Built in 1938, Oklahoma's eight-storey Jim Thorpe Memorial Office Building underwent a three-year, $70 million restoration; officials unveiled its Art Deco interiors in October 2026, with agencies returning this winter
articles.summary: Oklahoma has unveiled the restored Art Deco interiors of the Jim Thorpe Memorial Office Building after a three-year, $70 million renovation of the
articles.body: Oklahoma has unveiled the restored Art Deco interiors of the Jim Thorpe Memorial Office Building after a three-year, $70 million renovation of the eight-storey landmark in Oklahoma City. Built in 1938, the building has been modernised for public access, safety and agency operations while retaining signature features such as limestone walls, terrazzo floors, plaster ceilings and historic light fixtures. State leaders marked the completion with a ribbon-cutting on October 14, 2026, according to Oklahoma’s Office of Management and Enterprise Services. Read more details about it, as per the report, here:A historic building renewedThe Jim Thorpe Memorial Office Building has been part of Oklahoma’s Capitol Complex for more than eight decades. Originally called the State Capitol Office Building, it was renamed in 1961 in honour of Jim Thorpe, the Oklahoma-born Olympic athlete and one of the state’s most celebrated figures.By 2023, when the current renovation began, the building’s infrastructure needed extensive repair and modernisation. The project addressed long-standing problems including water infiltration, poor insulation and outdated layouts, while upgrading core building systems and installing energy-efficient windows designed to match the original appearance of the facade.The restoration was funded by state lawmakers through House Bill 1011X. Lawmakers also created the Jim Thorpe Repair Expenditure Oversight Committee through House Bill 1033X to review spending on interior and exterior repairs and provide public oversight as the work progressed through competitive procurement.Art Deco details preservedThe renovation focused as much on preservation as on modernisation. Project teams restored and protected defining Art Deco elements, including the building’s limestone walls, plaster ceilings, terrazzo floors and original light fixtures. These details help the renovated offices retain the architectural character of the late 1930s rather than becoming a generic government building.The building also retains important works of public art. In the lobby, 1930s-era bas-relief sculptures carved into the stone walls were carefully preserved, along with the exterior pediment sculpture above the east entrance. These works were co-created by Oklahoma art professors Doel Reed of Oklahoma State University and Joe Taylor of the University of Oklahoma, as per the report.New artworks were commissioned by the Oklahoma Arts Council under the state’s public art programme. The report also shares that Oklahoma artists Dr Jessica Moore Harjo and Erica Pretty Eagle Cozad created brass, copper and stainless steel ceiling installations for the first-floor corridors and sixth-floor elevator landing. Their designs use Sac and Fox motifs connected to the state flower, the state wildflower and the swan, a symbol of survival and resilience.Designed for modern governmentThe updated building is intended to make public services easier to access. Public-facing functions, including hearing and courtroom spaces, have been concentrated on the first floor, reducing confusion for visitors and improving accessibility.Behind the restored interiors, the renovation reconfigured older spaces for contemporary agency operations, public access and safety requirements. The eight-floor building now has the infrastructure needed to support modern state government while preserving the historic shell and architectural identity that make it distinctive.OMES Director Mark Wood said, according to the report, that the completed project honours the building’s historic character while providing the accessibility, infrastructure and functionality required for modern state government. He added that the agency was proud to guide the project from planning through completion.Agencies returning this winterFour state agencies will occupy the renovated building: the Oklahoma Corporation Commission, Oklahoma Arts Council, State Election Board and Oklahoma Water Resources Board. Their work covers areas that affect daily life across Oklahoma, including utilities, elections, the arts and water resources.The agencies will move in in phases beginning this winter. Once they are settled, the Jim Thorpe Memorial Office Building will return to its role as a central hub for essential public services within the Capitol Complex.Jim Marshall, interim director of the Oklahoma Corporation Commission and chair of the repair oversight committee, said the investment would make the building easier to access, more inviting and better equipped for the work ahead. His granddaughter, Anita Thorpe, said it was deeply meaningful to see his name continue to be honoured in a place dedicated to public service, describing the building as a reflection of strength, perseverance and pride.The new public art also connects the building to Thorpe’s Sac and Fox heritage and his Olympic legacy. With its Art Deco interiors restored and agencies preparing to return, the Jim Thorpe Memorial Office Building is set to serve Oklahomans for another generation.You use AI every day. articles.title: After 11 road accidents in four years, villagers in England spent four months knitting life-sized police officers and fake speed cameras; their handmade decoys are now making some drivers hit the brakes
articles.summary: A group of villagers in England has spent four months making something they hope will persuade speeding motorists to slow down: life-sized knitted traffic
articles.body: A group of villagers in England has spent four months making something they hope will persuade speeding motorists to slow down: life-sized knitted traffic officers and fake speed cameras. The unusual road safety campaign began after numerous accidents were recorded at a junction in Fillongley, Warwickshire, over four years. Since the handmade figures were installed last week, residents say they have noticed some drivers braking after mistaking them for real traffic enforcement equipment.According to BBC, members of the village's Knit and Natter group wanted to draw attention to a road safety problem that had troubled the community for years. That's when they decided to create figures that would be difficult for approaching motorists to ignore.Their work has appeared at several locations around Fillongley. Alongside the imitation traffic officers and speed cameras are knitted children carrying road safety messages and zebras placed above crossing signs. One figure, dressed in a Royal Air Force (RAF) uniform and a high-visibility vest, was also positioned beside the road holding a knitted speed gun.The campaign is particularly relevant to Nuneaton Road, where a busy crossroads has been a source of concern. Warwickshire County Council has recorded 11 traffic collisions at the junction over the past four years. A primary school is also located nearby. Residents say some drivers fail to pay attention to the speed limit signs, creating risks for people using the road.Why villagers decided to make their own traffic officersFor residents, the knitted figures are more than an attempt to amuse passing motorists. They are a response to continuing concerns about road safety and the time being taken to introduce permanent improvements.Heather Badham, 58, a parish clerk and member of the knitting group, believes drivers approaching the junction from Nuneaton Road are responsible for many of the accidents.Speaking to Good News Network, she said, "90% of the accidents are caused by people coming down the Nuneaton road, not seeing the signs and then hitting someone."The village already has a flashing 30mph speed limit sign. However, Badham said some motorists continue to travel too fast despite the warning.By making figures resembling officers monitoring traffic, they hoped to make approaching drivers more conscious of their speed.Their efforts appear to have produced the reaction they wanted, at least among some motorists. Badham said residents had watched vehicles slow down as drivers noticed the roadside displays."Since putting these up, we have been chuckling as people saw the man and thought he was real. You could see the brake lights coming on," she said.These observations suggest the figures have caught drivers' attention, although there is no evidence yet that the campaign has reduced the number of accidents.A four-month project attracts attention The figures have become a talking point among people living in the village. Their appearance is unusual enough to make some motorists look twice, while the messages carried by other knitted characters explain why the displays have been placed there.Local resident Tom Docker, 42, was among those surprised by the work. "I certainly did a double take when I saw the one with the camera. I couldn’t believe it," he told Good News Network. He praised the effort behind the creations and said they were encouraging people to discuss the problem of speeding.But the attention has not been entirely positive. One of the group's most distinctive figures, the knitted RAF officer, has disappeared.According to the BBC, the character was made in memory of the father of one of the knitters, who had served in the RAF during the Second World War. It had been dressed in a knitted high-visibility vest and given a handmade speed gun.Badham said the figure had apparently been stolen during a short period in the morning. Its disappearance upset the group, particularly because of the work involved in making it. "This is a piece of village heritage, and it's just been taken by somebody," she told the BBC. The group is considering making a replacement and reporting the matter to police.Village's road safety plansThe knitted campaign comes at a time when the future of the crossroads is already under discussion. Warwickshire County Council approved plans for traffic lights at the junction earlier this year. However, the proposal has not satisfied everyone. Some residents believe other measures, including average-speed cameras, should be considered.The council has said it is examining possible road safety improvements and waiting for confirmation from HS2 regarding funding for an alternative scheme.Warwickshire Police and Crime Commissioner Philip Seccombe has also recognised the seriousness of the problem, identifying Fillongley as one of the county's collision hotspots.You use AI every day. articles.title: Missile defence, Starlink support: Zelenskyy holds 'substantive' talks with Rubio amid Trump’s Russia shift
articles.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Tuesday said he held a \"substantive\" conversation with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio on ballistic missile
articles.body: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Tuesday said he held a "substantive" conversation with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio on ballistic missile defence, early warning of Russian attacks and the restoration of Starlink or Starshield services, as Kyiv seeks to strengthen its defences amid diplomatic efforts to end the war.Zelenskyy said the two sides discussed interceptors needed to counter Russian ballistic missiles, advance warnings of incoming attacks and the situation surrounding satellite services used by Ukraine’s military. They agreed to speak again soon for an update."I spoke with Marco Rubio, and it was substantive – on the issues that matter. I am grateful for the readiness to help and the clear position. First, interceptors against ballistic missiles, which are needed to protect lives. Second, early warning of Russian ballistic missile attacks, which is vital. Third, the situation surrounding Starlink/Starshield, which needs to be restored. Of course, all this is taking place against the backdrop of our diplomatic efforts to end this terrible war and the constant killing of people. We agreed to get in touch again soon for an update. Thank you, Marco, for being constructive! Thank you to everyone in America who supports fair approaches!"Zelenskyy shared the statement on social media on October 20.Starlink restrictions and missile warningsThe conversation comes amid concerns in Kyiv over disruptions to satellite support for Ukraine’s military and the availability of early warnings about Russian attacks.Starshield, a military-grade version of SpaceX’s Starlink satellite internet service, supports Ukraine’s drone operations and communications. Zelenskyy has said speed restrictions have affected Ukrainian drones’ ability to intercept Russian jet-powered drones.SpaceX chief Elon Musk has said Starshield is controlled by the US, with restrictions decided by the military and ultimately President Donald Trump. Trump, however, said he had not ordered restrictions and doubted that Musk had done so.Rubio said on Saturday that Ukraine wanted access to Starshield but did not have it. On Monday, he said the Pentagon controlled the system, adding that "Ukraine has benefited from it” and wants to expand its use for attacks beyond its territory. The US military has not publicly responded to questions about its role in the restrictions.Zelenskyy also said Kyiv had again received no early warning from partners, including the US, ahead of recent Russian attacks on Ukraine’s energy infrastructure.“Russia killed six people, including a mother and her child, who was just over a year old,” Zelenskyy said on X, adding that this "is how Russia responds to sanctions waivers and reduced pressure.”Trump and Rubio have maintained that Washington has not stopped providing intelligence to Kyiv to help it counter Russian attacks.US-Ukraine ties face fresh strainThe talks come as relations between Washington and Kyiv face renewed strain over the Trump administration’s approach to Russia and its support for Ukraine.Trump has recently rejected new sanctions on Russia and indicated he was open to talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping on ending the war. Asked whether he would negotiate an end to the conflict without Zelenskyy, Trump said: “I think it’s time for somebody else to negotiate on behalf of Ukraine.”The administration has also faced criticism over its decision to waive sanctions on Russia under legislation passed by Congress to restrict financial resources supporting Moscow’s war effort. A separate announcement on a deal to import Russian diesel fuel has drawn criticism from lawmakers who say it could benefit Russia without lowering global fuel prices.Former US ambassador to Ukraine John Herbst said Washington’s policy towards Moscow and Kyiv appeared to be at a low point.“At this moment in time, things look blacker than they ever had regarding this administration’s policy towards Russia and Ukraine,” said Herbst, now a scholar with the Atlantic Council.However, he said Trump could still change course. “Trump is a mercurial guy,” Herbst said. “He can wake up tomorrow morning, decide he’s done enough on this, and he might start to lean back in the other direction.”Former US ambassador to Poland Dan Fried said the administration’s recent decisions appeared aimed at putting pressure on Kyiv.“It all seems designed to put pressure on Zelenskyy and curry favor with Putin,” said Fried, now a scholar with the Atlantic Council.Lawmakers raise concerns over military supportThe dispute has also drawn criticism from US lawmakers, including Republicans, amid concerns over the impact of satellite restrictions and intelligence-sharing issues on Ukraine’s ability to defend itself.Pennsylvania Republican Representative Brian Fitzpatrick has called for congressional hearings into the Starshield disruptions and "immediate harsh and punitive budget cuts to any responsible agency or agency head.”Democratic Senator Richard Blumenthal said he and Republican Senator Thom Tillis had organised a call with Zelenskyy and a bipartisan group of lawmakers on Monday, including discussions about disruptions to US intelligence sharing.In a video of the briefing, Zelenskyy said Ukraine had “almost no Patriot interceptors left from the United States” and claimed “the Pentagon is delaying the delivery of missiles that our partners have already paid for.”Republican Senator Roger Wicker, chairman of the Senate Armed Services Committee, urged Trump to consider Zelenskyy’s offer to halt attacks on Russian energy infrastructure in exchange for US targeting assistance to counter Russian missiles.“President Trump can lower prices at the pump today by simply agreeing to this deal!” Wicker posted on X.The renewed diplomatic engagement with Rubio comes as Kyiv seeks continued US support for its air defences and satellite-based military operations while pursuing efforts to end the war.You use AI every day. articles.title: In the early 2000s, California man Elmer Long turned his father’s bottles into a public two-acre ranch; today, more than 200 welded trees display over 1,000 bottles
articles.summary: Explore Elmer Long's Bottle Tree Ranch, a spectacular two-acre display of over 200 metal trees adorned with 1,000 colorful bottles, located in Oro Grande, California. A tribute to his father's legacy and a must-see roadside attraction along Route 66.
articles.body: The Mojave Desert appears to be as desolate as it gets when you drive along the former National Trails Highway between Barstow and Victorville. Then there's a bottle forest at the side of the road. On a windy day, the entire area whistles as glass in every colour hangs from welded metal trees. It appears museum-worthy, but anyone can enter.This is Elmer’s Bottle Tree Ranch in Oro Grande, California, built using bottles his father collected and left behind. Long began creating bottle trees around 2000. Today, the free, two-acre site features more than 200 trees displaying over 1,000 bottles. Arts charity SPACES calls the place filled with hundreds of welded trees adorned with bottles and miscellaneous artefacts. The story behind the ranch begins with Long’s desert boyhood and his father’s collecting.A father’s desert hoardIn the 1950s, Elmer camped in the Mojave with his father, aircraft engineer Elmer Long Sr., who loved the desert. The two collected anything that caught their eye, including bottles, and noted where each find was located. The elder Long aged and began to pass out the bottles. His son chose to rescue the remains and transferred them to his house on Route 66 near Oro Grande. The bottles, metal pipes and antiques remained in storage until Long found a way to turn them into a display.From one tree to a forestAround 2000, Long attached bottles to a wooden post to create his first bottle tree. The following morning, sunlight shining through the glass inspired him to make more. Roadside America reports that travellers stopped to photograph the display that same day. By 2002, Long was creating bottle trees full-time. Long’s first bottle tree used a wooden post, but the ranch eventually grew into a forest of more than 200 trees made from metal pipes with welded branches, according to accounts from Amusing Planet.Bottles were just the start. The ranch also features a boat filled with bottles, a tree made from a discarded missile casing, and toppers ranging from an electric guitar and a surfboard to a gumball machine. The collection combines objects recovered from roadsides and landfills with decommissioned weapons and other military hardware documented in the SPACES archive.Long was not the first person to string bottles on trees in this part of the desert. Miles Mahan, a retired funfair worker, started creating Hula Ville in 1955 on a half-acre plot outside Hesperia, featuring bottle trees, painted rhymes and recovered signs. Some Route 66 writers have suggested that Hula Ville may have inspired Long, but the connection remains unconfirmed. Hula Ville was razed in September 1997, but some of it was spared and can be seen, SPACES notes, at the California Route 66 Museum in Victorville.Keeping the ranch standingElmer Long passed away on June 22, 2019, at the age of 72 after a battle with lung cancer. The ranch was reopened in early September of that year, with his son Elliott taking command. The ranch is free to enter when its gates are open, and a wishing well on the grounds accepts donations.Elliott has been upfront about how hard that is. He wrote on the ranch’s website that time, weather, neglect and the cost of keeping a property for free are catching up quicker than he can keep up. He estimated the deferred maintenance at roughly 150 hours of work, Route 66 News said. In an update in May 2026, he noted the gates have remained open largely thanks to a site manager named Brian and praised the additional travellers expecting when Route 66 hits its centenary.Route 66 turns 100 on 11 November 2026, which makes this a fitting moment to visit. The ranch sits at 24266 National Trails Highway in Oro Grande. There are no official hours, but the gates are usually open in daylight, and on days they are shut, you can still see much of it through the fence. Elmer Long never set out to create a monument. He had his father's bottles, some pipe put away and a post to try them on. What resulted was a free roadside attraction that drivers still stop to see.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Rihanna launched Fenty Beauty in 2017 with a 40-shade foundation range; years later, its co-owner began exploring a sale of its 50% stake
articles.summary: When Fenty Beauty arrived in 2017, one of its most talked-about features was something shoppers could see on the shelf: 40 foundation shades.
articles.body: When Fenty Beauty arrived in 2017, one of its most talked-about features was something shoppers could see on the shelf: 40 foundation shades. For customers who had spent years mixing products or leaving a shop without finding a close match, the range addressed a familiar problem. Rihanna had entered the cosmetics business in partnership with LVMH, the luxury group behind some of the world's best-known fashion and beauty names. The launch soon grew into a business of its own, separate from the singer's recording career. The ownership arrangement that helped bring it to market would come back into focus years later, when LVMH began exploring a sale of its half-share.Fenty Beauty entered the market with 40 foundation shades and a global launchFenty Beauty did not begin as a small local cosmetics line waiting to find an audience. Its September 2017 launch put the products in 1,600 stores across 17 countries. LVMH, Rihanna's business partner, brought experience in the luxury market, while the singer already had an international following. The scale of the release reflected both.The foundation collection drew particular attention. Forty shades gave shoppers a wider choice across fair, medium and deep complexions, including people who had often found the available options too limited. Other brands had worked on inclusive ranges before Fenty appeared, but the launch brought the issue into sharper public view. The phrase “Fenty effect” later came to describe the pressure on competitors to expand their own shade selections.How the business grew beyond Rihanna's music careerFenty Beauty found a commercial audience quickly. BBC reporting in 2021 put its sales at an estimated $100 million during the first 40 days after launch. Her connection to the products remained visible. Rihanna featured the brand on her social media accounts and spoke about its offerings, keeping Fenty in front of an audience that might otherwise have followed her mainly for music. The cosmetics business also gave her a source of wealth that did not depend on releasing albums or touring.Customers could buy Fenty through department stores and mainstream beauty retailers, including Boots in the UK. The products sat at a higher price point than some everyday make-up, but they were not confined to luxury department stores. That mix of positioning and availability helped the brand reach different groups of shoppers.By 2021, the scale of Rihanna's business interests was reflected in her estimated fortune. Forbes put her net worth at $1.7 billion, attributing about $1.4 billion to her interest in Fenty Beauty. Her other holdings included lingerie company Savage X Fenty, alongside earnings from music and acting. The figures showed just how much the cosmetics business had come to matter to her finances.How Rihanna and LVMH split ownership of Fenty BeautyRihanna and LVMH each held a 50% stake in Fenty Beauty, according to Forbes' 2021 reporting. The arrangement gave the singer a direct interest in the company while linking the brand to a group with an established presence in luxury goods and cosmetics.It was a different proposition from simply licensing a celebrity's name to a make-up line. Rihanna remained closely identified with the products, while LVMH was the corporate partner behind the business. Their interests had been joined at the brand's launch, and the equal split meant that any later decision to sell one side's stake could change the ownership arrangement without necessarily ending Fenty Beauty itself.Rihanna's Fenty Beauty partnership faces a potential turning pointYears after the launch, LVMH began exploring a possible sale of its 50% holding. The move put the company's ownership under scrutiny, but exploring a transaction does not mean that a deal has been completed. A confirmed buyer, an agreed price and the final terms would be separate steps.For Rihanna, Fenty Beauty had become one of the most substantial parts of her business portfolio since its debut. The 40-shade foundation collection helped establish its identity, and its early international rollout gave it reach beyond the singer's existing audience. What happens to LVMH's stake would determine whether the original partnership continues in its current form. Until a sale is confirmed, however, the reported exploration remains a possible change in ownership, not a completed one.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.summary: Entrepreneur Ashneer Grover recently took people inside DLF Camellias in Gurugram, offering a glimpse of a luxury residential complex.
articles.body: Entrepreneur Ashneer Grover recently took people inside DLF Camellias in Gurugram, offering a glimpse of a luxury residential complex. The society shot to fame for its INR 100-crore tag which is justified because of an exclusive clubhouse, an Olympic-sized swimming pool and a snow room too! The society is also known for its bowling alley and private movie theatre. It’s a tour that most were waiting for to understand why the development has become synonymous with ultra-luxury real estate in India.“It is a very private place. It doesn't look like India. You are paying premium for that,” Grover says in the tour video.The video was shared on YouTube by his wife, Madhuri Jain Grover, on October 17. Since then, it has drawn significant attention to one of the country's most expensive residential addresses. As per reports, some apartments here are valued at more than ₹100 crore.Inside the world of DLF CamelliasDLF Camellias is part of DLF's super-luxury residential portfolio. It is located on Golf Course Road in Gurugram and the project brings together high-rise residences, green surroundings, golf-course views. The extensive luxury facilities provided here are hard to find elsewhere, according to Grover.The official website of DLF mentions that the development features 16 towers ranging from 18 to 38 storeys, with the tallest reaching 156 metres.In his tour video, Grover shows several luxury facilities offered inside the society. These include an Olympic-sized swimming pool, fitness and wellness facilities, an indoor bowling alley, a snow room (which he says is his favourite), a world-class private cinema and spaces for dining and social gatherings.The scale of the clubhouse is particularly significant. Rather than treating recreational facilities as an add-on, the project integrates them into the residential experience, allowing residents to access leisure, entertainment and wellness amenities within the complex.Grover also highlighted the privacy and exclusivity which comes with such a price tag. For buyers spending tens of crores on a home, the appeal is not limited to interiors or square footage.The reason behind ₹100 crore valueAt this level of the market, the price of a property depends on several factors:LocationSizeConfigurationViewsDesignExclusivityLuxury amenitiesThe size and configuration of the residences also distinguish Camellias from conventional apartments. Large-format homes, duplexes and penthouses offer considerably more living space, while select residences benefit from expansive views and a more private residential setting.However, the reported ₹100-crore valuation is not a uniform price for every apartment.And that’s why Grover says they are ‘paying a premium’.More than just a homeOne of the most interesting parts of Grover's tour video is the way it presents the development as a destination in itself. There’s a clubhouse, different swimming pools, spa and sauna room, along with entertainment spaces. The piano room, fine-dining restaurant, and meeting space just add to overall appeal.For the luxury housing segment, such features add another dimension to the conversation around value, although the long-term performance of a property also depends on management standards, maintenance and continued demand.As India's wealthiest homebuyers seek increasingly differentiated residential experiences, projects such as DLF Camellias are setting new benchmarks for what developers can offer — and for how much buyers may be willing to pay. Ashneer Grover's reaction may have bought the development into limelight (once again), but it's story is more about a real estate sector changing the idea of what an exclusive home should offer.In Gurugram, that idea now extends well beyond the apartment door.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.body: NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder, Abhijeet Dipke, on Monday took a sarcastic dig at the planned burning of a 30-foot-tall cockroach effigy alongside Ravan during Dussehra celebrations on October 20 in Delhi, saying, “Thank you for the free publicity.”The Shri Keshav Ramlila Committee is set to burn the cockroach effigy alongside the traditional effigies of Ravana, Kumbhakarna and Meghnad at its grounds in Pitampura. The preparation for the event is underway, with the committee saying the initiative is intended to spread awareness about cleanliness and unhygienic conditions.What has the committee said?Ashok Goel Devaraha, president of the Shri Keshav Ramlila Committee and BJP MLA from Model Town, said the cockroach effigy was meant to symbolise filth and reinforce the message of the triumph of good over evil.Devaraha told ANI that the committee had previously burnt effigies representing issues such as Naxalism and terrorism. This year, it chose a cockroach to highlight the need to eliminate dirt and unhygienic conditions from homes, neighbourhoods and society.He also denied that the decision was politically motivated, saying the initiative aligned with the Swachh Bharat and Swachh Delhi campaigns.How did ‘cockroach’ become a political name?The planned effigy comes amid the rise of the satirical Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), a movement that emerged following remarks by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant during a Supreme Court hearing on May 15. The CJI had compared certain individuals with fraudulent degrees who become social media or RTI activists to “cockroaches” attacking the system.The remarks triggered a backlash among young people and inspired the CJP movement. The CJI later said his oral remarks had been “misquoted” and used with “malicious intent”.The CJP has since staged protests against former Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan and is now demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.Get the latest India News and Live updates.
